text: No, the 2019 loss should not be treated as evidence of deforestation. The Hansen data detected tree-cover loss in a planted forest area (Pinus elliottii/Pinus taeda), but the independent JRC 2020 reference contradicts this finding, showing no loss in the same area. The loss was likely a stand replacement (e.g., harvesting) rather than deforestation, as the context is a managed plantation. The evidence does not support deforestation or land-use change, only a temporary tree-cover reduction.
